beginner.summary: For Kubernetes users, platform engineers and developers who deploy applications on Kubernetes and are new to Istio. Covers the service mesh model, installing Istio with istioctl, sidecar injection with the Bookinfo and httpbin samples, north-south traffic through Gateway API and classic Istio gateways, VirtualService and DestinationRule routing, traffic shifting, request matching, timeouts, retries, fault injection and circuit breaking, automatic mTLS with PeerAuthentication, workload identity, AuthorizationPolicy and JWT RequestAuthentication, egress control with ServiceEntry, Prometheus metrics, Kiali and first-line debugging with istioctl, ending in a capstone that secures and releases Bookinfo.
prerequisites: Deploys and debugs applications on Kubernetes with kubectl: Deployments, Services, namespaces, labels and logs
Understands HTTP basics (methods, status codes, headers) and the idea of TLS certificates
Has a laptop with Docker or Podman, kind or minikube with at least 4 CPUs and 8 GB RAM free, kubectl, curl and rights to install istioctl
outcomes: Install Istio with istioctl, enable sidecar injection and explain how istiod, Envoy and gateways fit together
Route, split and harden traffic with Gateway API HTTPRoute, VirtualService and DestinationRule, including timeouts, retries, faults and circuit breakers
Enforce mutual TLS, AuthorizationPolicy and JWT validation, and control outbound traffic with ServiceEntry
Observe and debug a mesh with Prometheus metrics, Kiali, istioctl analyze and istioctl proxy-status

intermediate.summary: For engineers who already run Istio in sidecar mode and can route, secure and observe a single-cluster mesh. Covers ambient mode in depth (ztunnel, HBONE, istio-cni and waypoint proxies), migrating from sidecars to ambient, Gateway API for mesh traffic (GAMMA), gateway TLS termination, passthrough and TCP routing, egress gateways and TLS origination, OpenTelemetry tracing and the Telemetry API, locality failover, traffic mirroring, external authorization, plug-in CA certificates, Helm-based installation, canary control plane upgrades with revisions and tags, and Envoy and ztunnel troubleshooting, ending in a zero-downtime ambient migration capstone.
prerequisites: Completed the Istio beginner level or can install Istio and write VirtualService, DestinationRule, PeerAuthentication and AuthorizationPolicy resources
Comfortable with Helm, kubectl patch and rollout commands, and reading YAML diffs
Has a Kubernetes cluster with at least 3 nodes (kind multi-node is fine) and rights to install CRDs, DaemonSets and cluster-scoped webhooks
outcomes: Run workloads in ambient mode, add waypoint proxies only where L7 features are needed and migrate namespaces from sidecars without downtime
